title: Mohammed Waheed — Interim order review (2026-06-22)
text:
1

General Pharmaceutical Council

Mohammed Qasim Waheed

2236616

Pharmacist

Hannah Bows (Chair)

Kellie King (Registrant member)

Shaun Donnellan (Lay member)

Legal Adviser:

Austin Stoton
Secretary:

Gemma Staplehurst

Interim order being reviewed:

Interim conditions order
Outcome:

Interim conditions order continued

(with amendment to condition 3)

The Committee also considered the wording and scope of the third condition. It was concerned to
ensure that the condition was clear, workable and capable of being properly understood by the
Registrant, any employer, and those responsible for monitoring compliance. The Committee
therefore considered it necessary and proportionate to clarify the ambit of the condition so that
there could be no uncertainty about the type of setting in which face-to-face patient consultations
must not take place.

2

Order
1. You must:
a. give the GPhC the contact details of your place of employment and anyone who is likely to
be the manager or persons supervising you (employer, pharmacy owner, agency,
superintendent pharmacist, responsible pharmacist);
b. tell the GPhC before you take on any position for which you must be registered with the
GPhC;
c. give the GPhC details of the role and the hours you will work each week, including locum or
relief work;
d. tell the GPhC if any of the above details change.
2. You must notify the following people in writing of these conditions before you commence any
work, in relation to any paid or unpaid work for which registration with the GPhC is required:
- All employers or contractors
- Agents acting on behalf of employers and locum agencies
- Superintendent Pharmacists
- Responsible Pharmacists
- Line Managers
- Workplace supervisors
You must provide the GPhC with a copy of the notification(s).
3. You must not conduct any face-to-face patient consultation, or have any patient interaction, in
any private room, whether supervised, unsupervised, chaperoned, or unchaperoned. A “private
room” includes any enclosed or substantially enclosed room, office, consulting room, treatment
room, examination room, or other space where the consultation is conducted away from the
open public or pharmacy area and is not readily visible to other members of staff.
court: General Pharmaceutical Council — Fitness to Practise Committee
